subject.title: Gateway runtime: "no such table: plugin_state_entries / acp_sessions" despite tables existing in state/openclaw.sqlite (agent turns produce no reply)

question: Should maintainers require live path diagnostics before queueing a fix, or treat the report plus adjacent startup-migration merge as enough to start a Docker regression branch?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the observed contradiction depends on which database file the failing process actually opens at runtime; guessing the fix could add the wrong state compatibility behavior.

options.title: Collect Path Proof First
options.body: Ask for or run a redacted Docker repro that captures `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared-state database path, and `PRAGMA database_list` from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

options.title: Sponsor A Repro Branch
options.body: Use the report to build a focused Docker regression around gateway run, device-pair notify polling, `chat.history`, and `sessions.send`, then patch only after the mismatch is reproduced.

options.title: Retest Current Main First
options.body: Ask the reporter to retest a build containing https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101881 before deeper work, while keeping this issue open until the table errors are confirmed gone.

recommendation.title: Collect Path Proof First
recommendation.body: Ask for or run a redacted Docker repro that captures `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, resolved shared-state database path, and `PRAGMA database_list` from the failing gateway process before selecting the fix boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest feature-history ownership is on the shared SQLite state database and ACP metadata storage that both failing reads use.
